clue.text: Study coin classification, not allowing mind to wander

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
a cent is a small coin
a rating is a grading or classification

explanation.surface: A numismatist studies coin grades with unbroken attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' looks like the definition at the front, but it gives only the first piece; the definition is the closing phrase about the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Focusing hard means keeping attention fixed on one thing, never letting thoughts drift.

clue.text: Dictator's crank, working out alternative incentives

indicators.note: working out suggests the letters of Dictator's crank are solved into a new order

explanation.surface: A tyrant's eccentric devises a choice of motivations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working out' rearranges all fourteen letters of DICTATORS CRANK, the S included.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a mix of reward and punishment used to motivate, two options offered together.

clue.text: Valuable material smashed by crane

indicators.note: smashed means the word crane is broken and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Something precious is broken by a lifting crane.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother-of-pearl, the lustrous lining of shells, is prized for decoration.

clue.text: Outside in the Luxembourg gardens?

parts.note: the Jardin du Luxembourg is in Paris, so outdoors there would be put in French

explanation.surface: Being out of doors in a famous Paris park.
explanation.walkthrough: The Luxembourg gardens are in Paris, not Luxembourg, so the French phrase for outdoors fits; it is also the term for painting outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means in the open air, used of painting done outdoors.

clue.text: Call to embrace women and act like a star

indicators.note: to embrace means one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a tinkle is British slang for a phone call

explanation.surface: A phone call to hug the ladies and behave like a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give me a tinkle' is British slang for phone me. 'Star' suggests a celebrity, but it is a star in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Stars in the night sky shimmer and flicker with light.

clue.text: State in which no elephant will be seen?

definitions.text: State in which no elephant will be seen?

parts.words: State in which no elephant will be seen?
parts.note: elephants are said never to forget, so a condition of forgetting is one no elephant has

explanation.surface: A place where elephants never appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a country with no elephants; it is a condition. The saying is that an elephant never forgets.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of memory is a condition, the very thing elephants proverbially never suffer.

clue.text: Risky poem funny at the start and finish

parts.note: If is a famous poem by Rudyard Kipling

indicators.note: at the start and finish picks the first and last letters of the word funny

explanation.surface: A comic poem is a dicey venture at both ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If—' is Rudyard Kipling's well-known poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dodgy or uncertain is chancy, which is risky.

clue.text: Nil gaiety is very different from this

definitions.text: Nil gaiety is very different from this

indicators.note: very different from tells us the letters of nil gaiety are thoroughly rearranged

explanation.surface: Joylessness is the opposite of good cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is very different from' rearranges NIL GAIETY, and the whole clue also says what the answer is: a total absence of cheer is its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendliness and good cheer are the opposite of having no merriment at all.

clue.text: Huge car certain to look inappropriate for member of clergy

indicators.note: to look inappropriate suggests the letters of huge car certain are put out of place

explanation.surface: A vicar's enormous car is sure to seem unsuitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To look inappropriate' rearranges the fourteen letters of HUGE CAR CERTAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a priest responsible for a parish, a cleric by title.

clue.text: Somehow creep into party

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of creep into get there by some unspecified rearrangement

explanation.surface: A gatecrasher sneaks into a party unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges all nine letters of CREEP INTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A reception is a formal social gathering, such as one after a wedding.

clue.text: Adoring university food

parts.note: fond means loving or adoring

explanation.surface: A student is devoted to the food on campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondu is a variant spelling of fondue, the melted-cheese dish, so it is a kind of food.

clue.text: Huge gongs on middle of chest

parts.note: gongs is slang for medals or honours; OBEs are British honours

indicators.note: middle of picks out the central letter of the word chest

explanation.surface: Medals are pinned on the centre of a huge chest.
explanation.walkthrough: OBE is the Order of the British Empire, a British honour; 'gongs' is British slang for such decorations.
explanation.definitionFit: Grossly overweight people are very large, so huge is a loose synonym.

clue.text: Pet in truck is suffering

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words truck is suffering

explanation.surface: A pet animal shut in a lorry is in distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like an animal, but it is the verb to pet, to fondle or caress.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet someone is to cuddle and caress them, and to smooch is the same sort of affection.

clue.text: Celebration when a prisoner returns

indicators.note: returns asks for the words a prisoner, as letters, to be read backwards

parts.note: a lag is slang for a convict, as in old lag

explanation.surface: There is a party when a convict comes home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returns' reverses A plus LAG together, giving GAL A.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive occasion or special entertainment.

clue.text: Sort of name unusual for Cypriot man

indicators.note: unusual means the letters of Cypriot man are arranged unusually

explanation.surface: A strange name for a man from Cyprus.
explanation.definitionFit: A name taken from one's father's name, as in Russian Ivanovich, is a type of name.

clue.text: Forward movement very restricted in a waltz, say

indicators.note: restricted in means one letter is confined inside the words a waltz, say

parts.note: a waltz is an example of a dance, hence say

explanation.surface: Ballroom partners can barely move forward during a crowded waltz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restricted in' puts V inside A DANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An advance is progress or a move forwards, as of an army.

clue.text: Vehicle is landing on mercury, circling in and disappearing

indicators.note: landing on means the first pieces sit above the next in this down answer

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: circling means the mercury symbol goes round the next word

parts.note: Hg is the chemical symbol for mercury

explanation.surface: A spacecraft lands on Mercury, orbits and disappears from view.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'landing on' means sitting on top of what follows; 'circling' has the mercury symbol wrap round 'in'. The surface's spacecraft and planet Mercury are a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanishing means fading from sight, the same as disappearing.

clue.text: A king beset by a depravity - - greed

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the first pair of letters is enclosed by the second phrase

parts.note: a vice is a moral failing or depravity
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch is surrounded by corruption and covetousness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beset by' puts AR (A plus R for king) inside A VICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an extreme desire for wealth, which is greed by another name.

clue.text: Depression is beginning to threaten professional practitioner

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression in a surface

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the opening letter of the word threaten

explanation.surface: A slump starts to endanger a professional's practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' tempts as economic gloom; it is a physical dent.
explanation.definitionFit: A dental surgeon is a qualified professional who runs a practice treating teeth.

clue.text: Finished article almost completely coarse

indicators.note: almost completely says the article loses only its last letter

parts.note: the is the definite article
rough means coarse in texture

explanation.surface: The finished article is nearly all coarse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost completely' cuts the last letter off THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being done with something means you are over it, completed.

clue.text: Don't stop vehicle that is crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means the first two pieces span a further letter, which sits within them

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
yon is an old word for that, as in yonder

explanation.surface: A driver keeps going while the car fords a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossing' has the river's letter sit within the vehicle-plus-'that' pair; YON is an archaic word, as in yonder.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on is to continue, the opposite of halting.

clue.text: Happens to get some rioting in vessel

indicators.note: in means the scrambled letters go inside the vessel

parts.note: a cup is a drinking vessel

indicators.note: rioting suggests the letters of the word some run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: It happens that some people riot aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rioting' scrambles 'some' to OMES and 'in' sets it within the drinking vessel. 'Vessel' suggests a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: When something arises or crops up, it occurs.

clue.text: Job makes request after first sign of trouble

indicators.note: after says the request comes later than the opening letter
first sign of takes the opening letter of the word trouble

parts.note: to ask is to make a request

explanation.surface: A job begins when someone asks for help at the first hint of difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work to be done, a chore or assignment.

clue.text: Good butter — but not much of it?

parts.note: a butter is something that butts, and a ram butts with its head

explanation.surface: Fine butter, though only a scrap of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' is the spread on the surface, but here it is one who butts: a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: A gram is a tiny unit of weight, so a small amount of anything.

clue.text: Under poetic location in Wales

definitions.meaning: beneath, in its shortened poetic form

explanation.surface: Below lies a lyrical place in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Neath is a town near Swansea in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Poets clip beneath to one syllable with an apostrophe, and the same letters name a Welsh town.

clue.text: Old province featured in European journal

indicators.note: featured in means the letters appear inside the words European journal

explanation.surface: A former French region is the subject of a European periodical.
explanation.definitionFit: Anjou was a historic province of western France, around Angers.

clue.text: Radical being ignored?

definitions.meaning: politically radical, of the socialist wing

explanation.surface: An extremist is overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: The political wing of reformers is so named, and someone omitted has been passed over and abandoned.

clue.text: About to make oneself scarce when there's censure

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
to hide is to keep out of sight, making oneself scarce

explanation.surface: Someone about to flee when a reprimand is coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'About' alone gives C.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold someone is to censure or rebuke them.

clue.text: Right inside America, former PM stars

indicators.note: inside means one letter is put within America's abbreviation

parts.note: USA is the abbreviation for the United States of America
John Major was British Prime Minister from 1990 to 1997

explanation.surface: A right-winger inside America and an ex-premier are celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: John Major was a British Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Bear is a constellation, a group of stars.

clue.text: Understand what photographer may be sent out to do

definitions.meaning: to grasp or comprehend a situation

definitions.text: what photographer may be sent out to do
definitions.meaning: taken literally, a photographer is sent out to obtain an image

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to grasp the point, and literally a photographer's job is to come back with a photo.
